name: DeliberateActionProofV1

challenge.issue_rule: requires authenticated browser mutation context and action allowlisted by LLD-10 confirmation registry; target_type/id are stored as the exact DeliberateActionTargetV1 binding

complete: require same authenticated session/run and exact challenge id
require challenge state active and target/action inputs unchanged on client request
use SERVER time.monotonic_ns, not client-reported duration, to require elapsed >= 3_000_000_000 ns and <= 15 seconds
LLD-10 client state machine separately guarantees continuous pointer/touch/keyboard activation and cancellation semantics for deliberate_hold and impact_preview_plus_hold actions
atomically mark challenge completed and generate independent random 32-byte opaque proof token
store only SHA-256(proof token) with exact bindings; return token once

validate_and_consume: inside the owning command's existing UnitOfWork require current run/session binding, unexpired proof and constant-time token hash match
require expected action, exact DeliberateActionTargetV1, base_revision and preview_fingerprint exact equality

the owning domain command remains authoritative for guard ordering: it performs every business/dependency/freshness check that its contract requires before proof consumption; for tickets.rfc.terminal_cascade.execute this includes exact proposal/terminal/scope and both complete provider-impact revalidations plus reviewed preview-fingerprint equality
call validate_and_consume only at the owning command's specified deliberate-action boundary after all required pre-proof guards and before the protected authoritative mutation
atomically consume in memory before the protected domain mutation proceeds; failed transaction does not make proof reusable—operator repeats deliberate action
return ValidatedDeliberateActionV1 containing only the validated non-secret binding

cancel: LLD-10 release/Escape/route/target/dependency invalidation calls local cancellation or simply abandons challenge; expired/abandoned challenges are removed
rules: proof is friction evidence, not authorization and never replaces owning-domain eligibility/freshness guards
server elapsed minimum prevents instant completion requests but does not claim cryptographic proof of human intent
one completed hold produces at most one usable proof and one attempted owner command
LLD-12 does not impose proof-before-freshness ordering on owning domains; each owner contract defines the safe pre-proof guard boundary and validate_and_consume cannot be used to bypass it
